summary: Denmark’s country-specific conservation pledge is a 2030 LULUCF target of −441 kt CO2-eq, described as a 441 kt increase in net removals versus 2016–2018. National targets deliver the EU’s binding 310 Mt CO2 net-removal target (shown as −310 Mt in carbon-sink accounting), associated with 42 Mt of additional land-sector removals versus 2016–2018. Restoration is mainly EU-level: measures in at least 20% of EU land and sea areas by 2030, and in all ecosystems needing restoration by 2050. Cited EU mitigation potentials are 51–54 Mt CO2-eq/yr from peatland and wetland rewetting and 8–235 Mt CO2-eq/yr from a combined reforestation and sustainable forest-management measure; improved fertilizer-use efficiency could reduce 19 Mt CO2-eq/yr of nitrous oxide emissions. Except for Denmark’s 441 kt target, these figures are collective EU measures, not Danish coverage rates. Denmark’s 2022 cover is 71.6% agricultural, 11.4% forest, and 0.9% wetland.
